remainderRoutingAudit.whyThisWasTheRealTest: Every prior gate-row join in this sequence had a harness with no leftoverDesignRemaining list, so the inventory-short test had nothing concrete to bite on. G12 v4 does carry one — leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR114, nine entries — which is precisely the field whose two dropped members produced a blocker on the DR-105 join. So this was the one place the same defect could actually recur.
remainderRoutingAudit.routing: OBL-DOCTOR-FX-AUTHORING is carried as this join's own obligation at leftoverDesign true — correctly, since it is the doctor fixture authoring for G12's twelve FC classes and is the one item the dispatch's don't-steal list omits. Seven more — OBL-JOIN-FX-AUTHORING, OBL-JOIN-FX-EXECUTION, OBL-FC-C1 and OBL-BLK-1 through OBL-BLK-4 — are named in the guard obligation as remaining on DR-114, and I confirmed all seven are leftoverDesign true in doctor-actor-leftover-join.v6. That is eight of nine.
remainderRoutingAudit.theNinth: OBL-G21-HARNESS-SPEC is not named by id anywhere in the join. On its face that is the DR-105 shape. It resolved the other way at source. doctor-actor-leftover-join.v6 — the live DR-114 ledger, which the join pins by digest — carries OBL-G21-HARNESS-SPEC at leftoverDesign FALSE, with the reason that G21 is named and the specification now exists at harness.DR-G21.component-failure-containment.v3 at Claude ACCEPT 0/0. So its leftover-design closed after G12 v4 was written, and G12 v4's nine-item list is stale on exactly that entry.
remainderRoutingAudit.exactMatchAgainstTheCurrentLedger: v6's summary.leftoverDesign holds exactly eight ids, and they are exactly the eight the join's guard and its own obligation account for. Set-for-set identity. The join enumerates against the live ledger rather than replicating a superseded list, which is the stronger discipline.
remainderRoutingAudit.g21Handling: G21 is addressed by name three times as a takeover refusal rather than as a stolen leftover. That matches the dispatch's own decomposition, which separates 'Do not take over G21' from the don't-steal list, and it matches the corpus fact that G21's specification now exists and belongs to G21.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-three attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 5c354f68 at 0444, 12618 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778; live required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All nine cited pins reproduce, recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head, artifact and version are both 1, and file08StatusToken is the bare string OPEN matching the live DR-G12 gate row — an attack with particular force here because file 08 carries a SATISFIED row adjacent in the same table, and none of it leaked in. The join also quotes the assurance stage as SPECIFIED, which is right for this row and differs from the 'PROPOSED; not QUALIFIED' every sibling gate row carries, so a template copy would have been wrong. Two things made this subject different from its siblings and both were tested at source. First, the dispatch forbids inventing a leftoverNameNote as present on G12 v4. It is genuinely absent — that harness's whatThisCloses has exactly three keys and none is leftoverNameNote — and the join states the absence five times, grounding its standing instead on leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded, which does exist. Third instance of correct field-shape adaptation in this family. Second, and more consequential: G12 v4 is the first harness in this sequence to carry an explicit leftoverDesignRemaining enumeration, nine entries, which is exactly the field whose two dropped members produced a blocker on the DR-105 join. The join accounts for eight — one carried as its own obligation, seven named in the guard — and does not name the ninth, OBL-G21-HARNESS-SPEC, by id. On its face that is the DR-105 shape and I pursued it. It resolves the other way: doctor-actor-leftover-join.v6, the live DR-114 ledger the join pins by digest, carries OBL-G21-HARNESS-SPEC at leftoverDesign FALSE because harness.DR-G21.component-failure-containment.v3 now exists and closed it, and v6's summary.leftoverDesign is exactly the eight the join accounts for, set for set. G12 v4's nine-item list is the stale side. The join is enumerating against the current ledger rather than replicating a superseded list, and it handles G21 by takeover refusal three times, matching the dispatch's own decomposition. Filing that gap would have punished the join for being more current than the artifact it cites. The twelve FC classes are identical four ways, and the FC-D9 trap — a class name containing D9 where inventing a D9 code is forbidden — resolves the same way the DR-G10 one did: carried class name only, zero minted shapes, zero exit numbers. Bookkeeping reconciles at five and five. One disclosure beyond the usual: the twelve FC classes are the doctor fixture-class family whose input corpora I reviewed earlier in this session, six of whose verdicts remain unfiled because another lane's verdict occupies their write paths. I confirmed this join cites no doctor-fc-*-input-corpus artifact, so nothing here depends on a displaced verdict of mine — but a coordinator reconciling that collision should know which artifacts touch it and which do not.
